feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. This is the final iteration, so this feedback is for the record and for the team's understanding of the design. The Builder's geometry is the iteration 7 and 9 design, and I have adopted it unchanged. The controller I used is the iteration 9 controller (kd 0.375, kp 3.75, ki 0.21, base 1.15), because iteration 10 showed that lowering kd to 0.33 drops oval progress from 0.995 to 0.727 on the same geometry. Evidence: 60 mm span collapsed oval progress in iterations 3 (0.275) and 8 (0.301). The y 0.03 lead collapsed it in iteration 1 (0.273). The 16 mm footprint at 60 mm reached only 0.405 in iteration 2. Bend max_error has stayed on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau under every span, footprint, lead, wheel_track and controller change across iterations 0 to 10. Decide the next design as follows, if any further iteration occurs. If the oval holds at 0.95 or more and bend max_error stays on its plateau, test sensor y 0.04 with no other change, as the lead is the only untested sensing lever. If the oval falls below about 0.9, restore kd 0.375 before any geometry change. If the y 0.04 lead test fails, test a 16 mm footprint at the 50 mm span alone.
requested_changes: If the next race keeps oval progress at or above 0.95 and bend max_error on its plateau, test sensor y 0.04 on all five sensors with x at -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025 and 12 mm footprints. Do not go below y 0.04, because iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 collapses progress.

If the y 0.04 lead test does not bring bend max_error below 0.06 m, test sensor_size 0.016 at the 50 mm span with y 0.05 and wheel_track 0.10, run alone. Iteration 2 gave oval progress 0.405 with 16 mm footprints at 60 mm, so this is a lower-priority test.
Keep the 50 mm span (x = -0.025 to 0.025) and wheel_track 0.10. Iterations 4, 7 and 9 held oval progress at 0.71 or above at 50 mm, and iterations 3 and 8 show that 60 mm collapses it.
